# Task
Deliver a proven authorization policy consistency loop: {task}

# Done When
- Policy Builder builds the smallest shared policy decision and leaves permission matrix, role/resource/field contract, policy-decision trace, cache / rollout impact, and unproven claims.
- Contract Inspector and Security Evidence Inspector read the same Builder handoff in one parallel_group. Contract Inspector verifies the matrix, SCIM/SSO mapping, policy version rollout, cache invalidation, and backward compatibility.
- Security Evidence Inspector independently attacks negative authorization, cross-tenant escalation, stale cache / revocation, export/report, background job, field-level leakage, and audit evidence.
- Authorization GateKeeper finishes only when authorization-policy, tenant-isolation, permission-auth, cache-invalidation, data-export, audit-log, and local-governance evidence prove the task claims.

# Guardrails
- Do not expand into a generic RBAC rewrite, SSO rewrite, audit-only, export-only, or UI-only permission polish.
- Hidden-buttons-only, middleware-only, admin-happy-path-only, API-only, missing negative authorization, missing field-level proof, missing stale-cache/revocation proof, or skipped local governance must fail closed.
- Do not claim a policy engine, tenant model, cache layer, SCIM/SSO provider, audit writer, or test runner was observed unless verified in the workdir.

# Success Surface
- Users can audit role/resource/field permission matrix, policy-decision trace, API/UI/job/export consistency, SCIM/SSO mapping, policy version rollout, and cache invalidation.
- Users can see cross-tenant escalation, stale cache / revocation, field-level leakage, background job bypass, export/report leakage, audit gaps, and each claim's evidence bucket.

# Fake Done
- Hidden buttons, middleware-only checks, admin happy path, API-only proof, or permission docs do not pass.
- Missing negative authorization, cross-tenant, field-level, background job, export/report, cache revocation, audit, or local-governance evidence does not pass.

# Evidence Preferences
- Prefer permission matrix fixtures, policy-decision traces, negative authorization cases, cross-tenant samples, field-level leakage tests, stale cache / revocation checks, export/report negatives, background job checks, audit refs, and compatibility proof.
- Both parallel Inspectors must mark thin evidence as Weak, unsupported claims as Unproven, closure blockers as Blocking, and non-core matrix polish as Residual risk.
- GateKeeper verdict must cite upstream handoffs, evidence refs, or artifacts, not only a final narrative.

# Execution Strategy
Use Policy Builder -> [Contract Inspector + Security Evidence Inspector] -> Authorization GateKeeper. Both Inspectors read the Builder handoff in one parallel_group; GateKeeper combines both inspection handoffs and evidence_query before judgment.

# Judgment Tradeoffs
Authorization consistency, negative samples, tenant isolation, field-level protection, cache/revocation, and audit proof beat faster UI permission polish. Speed cannot hide hidden-buttons-only, middleware-only, or admin-happy-path-only proof.

# Residual Risk
Minor policy matrix documentation cleanup may remain only with owner/follow-up. Missing negative authorization, tenant isolation, field permissions, export/job/cache/audit, or local-governance evidence must fail closed.

# Role Notes
## Policy Builder Notes
Build the smallest shared policy decision and leave permission matrix, policy-decision trace, changed surfaces, evidence, and unproven claims.

## Contract Inspector Notes
Read-only verify permission matrix, role/resource/field contract, SCIM/SSO mapping, policy version rollout, cache invalidation, and backward compatibility.

## Security Evidence Inspector Notes
Independently attack negative authorization, cross-tenant escalation, stale cache / revocation, export/report, background job, field-level leakage, and audit evidence.

## Authorization GateKeeper Notes
Judge from Builder, both parallel inspection handoffs, and evidence_query; fail closed unless core authorization claims are Proven.

# Authorization Policy Workflow Notes
- This authorization policy task refines the generic execution strategy: Policy Builder builds only the smallest shared policy decision and leaves permission matrix, policy-decision trace, changed surfaces, and unproven claims.
- Contract Inspector and Security Evidence Inspector must read the same Builder handoff in one parallel_group; Contract Inspector verifies permission matrix, role/resource/field contract, SCIM/SSO mapping, policy version rollout, cache invalidation, and backward compatibility.
- Security Evidence Inspector independently attacks negative authorization, cross-tenant escalation, stale cache / revocation, export/report, background jobs, field-level leakage, and audit evidence.
- GateKeeper must read both parallel handoffs and judge authorization-policy, tenant-isolation, permission-auth, cache-invalidation, data-export, audit-log, and local-governance through evidence_query; hidden-buttons-only, middleware-only, admin-happy-path-only, or API-only evidence must fail closed.
